p: The park sits a couple of miles south of Burford off the A361, which puts you right in the middle of some of the loveliest countryside in the Cotswolds. It's easy to fill a weekend without driving far.

In Burford, the parish church of St John the Baptist is well worth a look. In 1649 a group of Levellers, mutinous soldiers from Cromwell's army, were locked up inside it, and one of them carved his name into the font; you can still see it. Follow the River Windrush east and you'll reach Minster Lovell, where the ruins of a fifteenth-century manor house sit by the water, free to explore and very atmospheric. The tiny village of Swinbrook, close by, has a riverside pub and the graves of several of the famous Mitford sisters in its churchyard.
Head west and Bibury, with its row of weavers' cottages at Arlington Row, is one of the most photographed spots in the Cotswolds. It gets busy, so early or late in the day is best.

At the park, keep an eye out for the walk-through areas where you can get closer to some of the smaller residents, and leave time for a sit-down in the gardens. On sunny days, the lawn in front of the house is perfect for a picnic with a view of the rhinos.
